title: Booking Appointments
text: Appointments · Booking Appointments · 8 min read · A step-by-step guide to booking, rescheduling and managing patient appointments — using the doctor's live schedule, 15-minute slots, and the full 4-status workflow built into the platform. · What you'll learn · Open the Appointments Screen · Same flow for clinic owners, receptionists & doctors · From the sidebar click · and then · + New Appointment · . The list shows you a snapshot of today's appointments with quick filters for status, doctor and date range. · Tip: · Need to register a walk-in instead? Use the · Walk-in · screen — it skips slot selection and books the patient into the next available time. · Select the Patient · Returning patient or instant new registration · Start typing the patient's name or phone in the · patient search · . Matching records appear instantly so you can pick a returning patient with one click — their full history follows them into the appointment automatically. · If the patient isn't in your system yet, click · + Add New Patient · inline. Capture name, phone, gender and date of birth — that's enough to book. You can fill in the rest of the profile later from their patient page. · Pick Doctor, Date & 15-Minute Slot · Live availability — never double-book · Choose the doctor and date. The platform reads the doctor's · weekly schedule, break times and leaves · and only shows · available 15-minute slots · for that day. Slots already taken are hidden, and the system blocks bookings that would clash with existing appointments. · Add the · reason for visit · and (optionally) the consultation · fee · — the fee defaults to the doctor's standard charge but you can override it for follow-ups or discounts. · Confirm & Save · Status: Scheduled · Click · Book Appointment · . The new entry appears immediately on the appointments list, the doctor's calendar, and the patient's timeline with status · Scheduled · . Receptionists assigned to that doctor see it the moment they refresh. · The 4-Status Workflow · From booked all the way to completed · Every appointment moves through one of four statuses. text: For Clinics · Setting Up Specializations · 6 min read · Specializations power your entire doctor catalogue — they decide which specialties patients can browse, how doctors are filtered when booking appointments, and which doctors appear on your public clinic page. Here's how to set them up the right way. · What you'll learn · Why specializations matter · specialization · (Cardiologist, Dermatologist, Gynaecologist, ENT Specialist, etc.) is the single most important attribute on a doctor's profile. You'll see the full list of every specialty currently available inside your clinic, a count badge, a live search box and the · + Add Specialization · button at the top right. · Who can edit? · Only the Clinic Owner manages specializations. A small dialog appears with a single field — the specialization · name · . title: Managing Your Schedule
text: For Doctors · Managing Your Schedule · 7 min read · Your schedule is the heart of your practice on the platform — it controls which days and hours you're available, your daily break time, and any upcoming leaves. Everything you set here directly drives the appointment slots patients (and your receptionist) can book. · What you'll learn · Why your schedule matters · Your weekly availability and leaves are the · single source of truth · used everywhere on the platform — your public profile, the booking dialog, the clinic dashboard and the receptionist's walk-in screen all read from the same schedule. If a slot isn't on your schedule, no one can book it. If it is, it auto-appears in · 15-minute intervals · Open the Schedule Screen · Sidebar → My Schedule · From the doctor sidebar click · My Schedule · . You'll see two tabs: · Weekly Hours · (Sunday → Saturday) and · Leaves · . Clinic Owners can also reach this screen for any of their doctors via · Doctors → Schedules · On mobile? · The same controls live under · More → Schedule & Leaves · in the Zonoir app. · Set Weekly Working Hours · One row per day, toggle + start/end time · Each day of the week has its own row with an · Available · toggle. Switch it on for working days and pick your · start · and · end · times. Switch it off to mark the day as a weekly off — that day will stop showing in the booking dropdown immediately. · Click · Save schedule · at the bottom to commit. Existing future appointments are · not · deleted — only new bookings are affected. · Add a Daily Break · Lunch, prayer or any midday gap · Inside each day's card you can also set an optional · break start · break end · . Slots that fall inside the break window are automatically removed from the booking grid, so patients can't book over your lunch or prayer time. · Add Leaves (Full or Half Day) · For travel, conferences or sick days · Switch to the · tab and click · + Add leave · . Pick a date, choose the type and optionally add a reason: · Full day · — entire day blocked, no slots offered. · Morning (Half day) · — morning slots blocked, afternoon stays open. · Evening (Half day) · — afternoon/evening slots blocked, mornings stay open. · Leaves immediately reflect on your public profile's weekly schedule (greyed-out days), the booking dialog and the clinic calendar. Remove a leave anytime with the trash icon — slots reopen instantly. · Already-booked appointments are not auto-cancelled · when you mark a leave. Open the appointment list and reschedule or cancel them manually so patients are notified properly. · How 15-Minute Slots Are Generated · It all happens automatically · Once your weekly hours, breaks and leaves are saved, the platform generates bookable slots in · between your start and end times — skipping breaks, leaves and any slot already booked. There's nothing else to configure: edit the schedule, save, and the booking experience updates everywhere within seconds. · Edit on the Go (Mobile App) · Same controls, native experience · The Zonoir mobile app mirrors the web schedule screen 1:1. Open · , flip the day toggles, set your hours, tap · , and add leaves from the bottom sheet. Useful when you're between consultations and need to block off a sudden afternoon. · Best Practices · • Keep weekly hours · realistic · — overcommitting leads to overbooked days · • Always set a · break window · so patients don't book your lunch slot · • Add planned leaves · well in advance · — patients can't book leave dates the moment you save · Reschedule existing appointments · after marking a leave — the leave only blocks future bookings · • Use · half-day leaves · for short personal commitments instead of blocking the whole day · • Review your schedule once a week to keep your public profile accurate · Was this article helpful? · Yes, it helped · No, I need more help · Related Articles · Per-day start / end times · Break Time · Daily lunch / prayer break · Full-day & half-day off · Booking Appointments · Adding Doctors

text: For Doctors · Creating Prescription Templates · 7 min read · Save hours every week by building reusable prescription, test, report, and leave templates — then apply them to any patient visit with a single click. · What you'll learn · Why use prescription templates? · once · and reuse it instantly, while still allowing patient-specific tweaks before printing. · The five template types · Inside · Templates · in your sidebar, you'll find five tabs. text: For Clinics · Managing Doctor Limits & Capacity Increase · 5 min read · Understand how doctor limits work, monitor your clinic's capacity, and request an increase when you are ready to grow. · What you'll learn · How Doctor Limits Work · Understanding your clinic's capacity · When you sign up your clinic, you choose how many doctors you plan to add to the system. Please increase your capacity to add more doctors." · Important: · Deleting an active doctor frees up one slot in your limit, but the doctor's historical data (appointments, visit records, prescriptions) is retained for compliance purposes. · Requesting a Capacity Increase · Growing your clinic on the platform · To increase the number of doctors your clinic can support, you need to update your · value. Currently, this is handled directly by our support team to ensure accurate billing adjustments. · Increase Limit · Contact support with your desired new doctor count. Your billing is prorated so you only pay for the extra doctors from the day the change is applied. · Billing Impact of Adding Doctors · How your subscription cost changes · Your subscription fee is calculated · per doctor, per billing period · . text: For Doctors & Clinics · Importing & Exporting Patients (CSV) · 6 min read · Bulk upload existing patient records or download your full patient list for backups, reporting, and external use. · What you'll learn · Exporting Patients · Download your patient list as a spreadsheet · Both clinics and individual doctors can export their patient records to an Excel file. The system accepts Excel (.xlsx) and CSV files. · Step-by-step import process · 1. Download the Sample File · On the Patients page, open the Import/Export dropdown and click Download Sample Excel. The system reads the file and shows a preview before saving. · Success: · After a successful import, the Patients list refreshes automatically and you will see a toast notification confirming how many records were added. · Required & Optional Columns · What your spreadsheet must contain · The import engine expects specific column names. Missing required fields will cause that row to be rejected. Optional fields can be left blank. · Required · Optional · Important: · Do not change column headers or add extra columns. The importer matches columns by exact name. If a required field is missing or invalid, that entire row is skipped and reported in the error summary. · Duplicate Detection · How the system prevents duplicate patient records · Before creating any patient during import, the system checks for existing records that share the same phone number or CNIC. This prevents your database from filling with duplicates. · Phone Number Match · If a patient with the same phone number already exists, the importer flags the row as a duplicate. You can review matched patients before deciding to skip or proceed. · CNIC Match · If CNIC is provided and matches an existing record, the row is also flagged. Both phone and CNIC are normalized during comparison so formatting differences do not matter. · Always include phone numbers in your import file. Phone is the most reliable unique identifier in the system and triggers the strongest duplicate protection. · Common Errors & Fixes · What to do when an import fails · Best Practice: · Before importing hundreds of rows, test with 5-10 rows first. title: Avoiding Duplicate Patient Records
text: For Clinics · Avoiding Duplicate Patient Records · For Clinics & Doctors · 5 min read · Learn how the system detects and prevents duplicate patients using Contact Number and CNIC matching — and what to do when a duplicate warning appears. · What you'll learn · Why Duplicates Matter · Duplicate patient records fragment medical history, make prescriptions harder to track, and inflate your patient count. The system automatically checks for duplicates whenever a new patient is added — by hand or via CSV import. · How Duplicate Detection Works · Automatic matching on Contact Number and CNIC · The system checks for duplicates by comparing two key identifiers: · Contact Number Match · If the phone number you enter already belongs to an existing patient, the system flags it as a duplicate. Spaces and dashes are ignored during comparison. · CNIC Match · If a CNIC (National ID) is provided and it matches an existing record, the system raises a duplicate warning regardless of the phone number. · Normalization: · Before comparison, the system strips all spaces and dashes from phone numbers and CNICs. This means · , and · are treated as identical. · Duplicate Warning During Manual Entry · What happens when adding a patient by hand · When you create a new patient from the · Patients · page or during a · Walk-In · , the system runs a real-time duplicate check before saving: · Pro Tip: · Always prefer updating an existing patient's record rather than creating a duplicate. Use the search box on the Patients page to find the original record quickly. · Duplicate Detection in CSV Imports · How bulk import handles duplicates · When importing patients via Excel/CSV, the system performs a two-level duplicate check: · Within-File Duplicates · The importer scans your spreadsheet for duplicate rows before touching the database. Matches are skipped and reported in the import summary with the reason. · After the import completes, you will see a summary: · Imported: · Number of new patients successfully added · Skipped: · Number of rows ignored due to duplicates or validation errors · Tip: · Download the sample Excel template before importing. title: Understanding 15-Minute Appointment Slots
text: Appointments · Understanding 15-Minute Appointment Slots · 6 min read · Learn how our 15-minute time slot system works, why it keeps your clinic schedule efficient, and how it adapts to each doctor's availability, leaves, and existing bookings. · What you'll learn · The 15-Minute Grid · How time is divided across the day · Our platform divides every day into · 15-minute intervals · — from 00:00 (midnight) to 23:45. This fine-grained grid gives you maximum flexibility when booking appointments, whether a consultation takes 15 minutes or a full hour. · Sample morning slots — each cell represents one 15-minute block · When you open the time selector on the booking screen, you see only the slots that are · actually available · for the chosen doctor and date. The list is filtered in real time so you never accidentally double-book. · Pro Tip: · If a doctor usually needs 30 minutes per patient, simply book two consecutive 15-minute slots. The system will block both, preventing overlaps. · Doctor Schedules Filter the Grid · Availability is driven by weekly schedule settings · Before any slots are shown, the system checks the doctor's · weekly schedule · . Each day of the week can have its own start time, end time, and on/off toggle. · Example · Dr. Ayesha is scheduled Monday–Friday from 09:00 to 14:00. On Tuesday, a patient opens the booking calendar — only slots between 09:00 and 14:00 are listed, in 15-minute steps. · Leaves Remove Slots Automatically · Full-day and half-day leave handling · When a doctor adds a leave entry, the system immediately recalculates available slots for that date: · Full-Day Leave · All slots for the day are removed. Patients see "Doctor not available" instead of a time list. · Half-Day Morning · Slots before 12:00 are hidden. Afternoon slots (12:00 onwards) remain bookable. · Half-Day Evening · Slots from 12:00 onwards are hidden. Morning slots (before 12:00) remain bookable. · Tip: · Leaves can be added from the doctor's dashboard under · Schedule > Manage Leaves · . The change is instant — no cache delay. · Booked Slots Are Blocked · Real-time conflict prevention · Once an appointment is confirmed for a specific doctor, date, and time, that 15-minute slot is · automatically excluded · from the selector. Cancelled and completed appointments do not block the slot — only active/upcoming bookings count. · Active / Pending · These statuses block the slot. No other patient can be booked at the same time. · Cancelled / Completed · These statuses free the slot. A cancelled slot becomes available for re-booking immediately. · Editing an Appointment · When you edit an existing appointment and change its time, the old slot is released and the new one is checked for conflicts before saving. This prevents accidental double-booking during rescheduling. · Optimizing Your Daily Flow · Best practices for clinic efficiency · The 15-minute grid is designed to be flexible. Here is how clinics get the most out of it: · Receptionists can see a live calendar view that highlights booked, available, and leave-blocked slots in different colors. Use this visual overview to spot gaps and suggest alternate times to patients quickly. · Important Notes · • Slots are generated in 15-minute intervals across the full 24-hour day · • A doctor's weekly schedule is the first filter applied to the raw grid · • Full-day and half-day leaves override the schedule for that specific date · • Only active/pending appointments block a slot; cancelled ones free it immediately · • Each doctor has an independent slot pool — bookings for Dr. A do not affect Dr. B · Was this article helpful? · Yes, it helped · No, I need more help · Related Articles · Working Days · Only days marked 'Available' show slots. · Start & End Time · Slots outside working hours are hidden. · Day Off · If a day is toggled off, no slots appear at all. · Per-Doctor · Each doctor has an independent schedule. · Back-to-Back Booking · Book consecutive slots for longer procedures (30 min = 2 slots, 45 min = 3 slots). · Buffer Time · Leave one 15-minute gap between heavy cases to avoid running late. · Walk-in Buffer · Keep a few unbooked afternoon slots for urgent walk-ins. · Rapid Consults · For follow-ups that take 5–10 minutes, one slot is usually enough. · Booking Appointments · Managing Your Schedule · Managing Leaves (Full-Day & Half-Day) · Setting Weekly Availability & Break Times

title: The 4 Appointment Statuses Explained
text: Appointments · The 4 Appointment Statuses Explained · 5 min read · Understand how Scheduled, Started, Completed, and Cancelled work together to keep your clinic organized and conflict-free. · What you'll learn · Every appointment on the platform moves through a simple but powerful status workflow. These four states — · Scheduled · Started · Completed · , and · Cancelled · — are designed to keep your calendar accurate, your patient flow smooth, and your reporting reliable. · The appointment is booked and the slot is reserved · is the starting state of every new appointment. When a receptionist or doctor creates a booking — whether for a future date or a same-day walk-in — the appointment is created with this status. · Slot Blocking · A Scheduled appointment blocks its 15-minute slot. No other patient can be booked at the same doctor, date, and time. · Who Can Create · Receptionists, clinic owners, and doctors can all create Scheduled appointments from their respective dashboards. · Tip: · Use the Calendar view to see all Scheduled appointments at a glance. Scheduled bookings appear with a blue indicator so receptionists can quickly spot upcoming visits. · The patient has arrived and the consultation is in progress · When the patient arrives and the doctor begins the consultation, the status is updated to · . This is a critical transition — it records a timestamp and signals that the doctor is currently occupied. · Timestamp Recorded · The exact time the status changes to Started is saved automatically. This helps track actual wait times and consultation duration. · Slot Remains Blocked · The 15-minute slot stays reserved while the appointment is Started. Other patients cannot be booked into this time. · How to Mark as Started · Receptionists and doctors can change the status from the appointment list or calendar view. Bulk actions are also supported — select multiple appointments and mark them all as Started in one click. · The consultation is finished and the slot is released · Once the doctor finishes the visit — vitals recorded, prescription written, notes saved — the appointment is marked · . This finalizes the encounter and frees the time slot for future bookings. · Slot Released · A Completed appointment no longer blocks its 15-minute slot. A single leak can destroy years of trust and expose your clinic to legal action. Zonoir is built from the ground up assuming that · every record is confidential by default · , and that no doctor, no receptionist, and no other clinic should ever see data that doesn't belong to them. · This article explains, layer by layer, exactly how that protection works — so you can confidently answer the question every serious patient eventually asks: · "Is my information safe with you?" · 1. Encryption — your data is unreadable to outsiders · In transit (between your browser and our servers) · Every page on Zonoir is served over · HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ · . The padlock in your browser is not decorative — it means data travelling between your device and our servers is encrypted and cannot be read by anyone sitting on the same Wi-Fi network. · HSTS is enforced on the production domain, so browsers refuse to fall back to insecure HTTP even if someone tries to trick them. · Video consultations use Daily.co's SRTP-encrypted media streams — the call itself is encrypted end-to-end between participants. · At rest (on our database servers) · The underlying PostgreSQL database is encrypted at rest using · AES-256 · , the same standard used by banks and governments. · File uploads (lab reports, scans, prescription PDFs) live in encrypted object storage with signed, time-limited URLs — links you share expire automatically. · Database backups are also encrypted before they're written to disk and replicated across regions. · Plain English: · Even if someone physically stole a hard drive from our datacenter, the contents would look like random gibberish without the encryption keys. · 2. Row-Level Security — every clinic is an island · This is the single most important technical safeguard in Zonoir. Every table that contains patient data has · Row-Level Security (RLS) policies · enforced directly inside the database. This means access rules are not just checked by our application code — they are checked by PostgreSQL itself on every single query. · What RLS guarantees · A doctor logged into Clinic A · cannot · read, write, or even know about patients belonging to Clinic B. The database itself refuses to return those rows. · A receptionist at Clinic A can only see appointments and patients for the doctors and locations they are assigned to. · A single-doctor account (no clinic) is fully isolated — their patients are tied to · created_by = doctor_id · and no other account can query them. · Even if a bug in our application accidentally tried to fetch the wrong data, the database would return · zero rows · instead of leaking anything. · How permissions are structured · Role · Can see · Cannot see · Clinic Owner · All doctors, patients, finance, reports for their clinic · Any data from another clinic · Doctor (in a clinic) · Their own appointments, their patients, their prescriptions · Other doctors' private notes; clinic financials (unless granted) · Receptionist · Appointments, basic patient info, billing for assigned doctors · Clinical notes the doctor marks private; admin settings · Patient (public booking) · Only their own appointment confirmation · Everything else — no login required, no data exposed · 3. Authentication — only the right humans get in · Login security · Passwords are · never stored in plain text · . They are hashed using bcrypt before they ever touch our database — even Zonoir engineers cannot read your password. · Zonoir has · Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) checks · enabled at signup and password change. If you try to use a password that has appeared in a known data breach, the system refuses and asks you to pick a stronger one. · Sessions use signed, short-lived JWT tokens that refresh automatically. Logging out on one device invalidates that session immediately. · Password reset links are · single-use and time-limited · . Inactive or unapproved accounts cannot trigger resets — preventing pre-approval account takeover. · Account lifecycle controls · New doctors added by a clinic stay in a · pending / unapproved · state until the clinic owner explicitly approves them. An unapproved doctor cannot access any patient data. · Receptionists can be set to · active · or · draft · at any time — toggling to draft instantly cuts off their access without deleting their history. · Clinics that fall behind on payments move to an · inactive · status, which is checked on every login. · 4. Audit logs — every important action is recorded · Trust requires accountability. Zonoir maintains an · Activity Log · that records who did what and when — so if a record changes, you always know which user made the change from which session. · Patient creation, edits, and deletions · Appointment status changes (started, completed, cancelled) · Prescription creation and edits · Login events and password resets · Doctor approvals, receptionist additions, role changes · Inventory adjustments and financial transactions · Clinic owners can view activity logs from the dashboard at any time. Logs are append-only — even an admin cannot quietly rewrite history. · 5. Backups & disaster recovery · Automatic daily backups · of the entire database, encrypted and stored separately from the production database. · Point-in-time recovery · available for the last 7 days — we can restore your clinic's data to any specific moment if something goes catastrophically wrong. · Backups are tested regularly. A backup you can't restore is just expensive disk space. · File uploads are stored on redundant object storage with versioning, so accidental deletions can be recovered. · What this means for you: · If a doctor accidentally deletes a year of visit notes, or a hard drive fails on our side, your data is recoverable — usually within hours, not days. · 6. Edge function security — protecting the moving parts · Some features — sending contact emails, generating AI summaries, running AI prescription suggestions — run inside isolated · edge functions · . These are hardened with several layers of protection: · CORS allowlist · : only requests from · zonoir.com · and approved preview domains are accepted. Random websites cannot call our APIs. · Sliding-window rate limiting · : prevents abuse, bot floods, and runaway costs. · CAPTCHA verification · on public forms (contact form, public booking) to block automated submissions. · Server-side API keys · : Gemini, Resend, Daily.co, and Stripe keys live only in secure server environments — they are never shipped to your browser, never visible in network tabs, never leakable through "View Source". · Generic error messages · : when something fails, users see "Something went wrong" instead of database internals that could help an attacker. · 7. AI features — privacy by design · Zonoir's AI tools (Prescription Assistant, Visit Summaries, Patient Insights, Revenue Forecasts, Doctor Finder) are built with strict guardrails: · AI requests are · scoped to the calling user's clinic · — the model never receives data from clinics outside your account. · The AI provider (Gemini via Lovable AI Gateway) operates under a · no-training agreement · : your patient data is not used to train public models. · AI suggestions are clearly labelled and require · doctor review · before they become part of the medical record. text: Account & Security · User Roles & Permissions Explained · 9 min read · For Clinic Owners & Admins · Zonoir uses a strict role-based access control (RBAC) model so every staff member sees exactly what they need — and nothing they don't. This guide walks through every role, what they can do, and how to choose the right one. · What you'll learn · Why roles matter · In a real clinic, a receptionist doesn't sign prescriptions, a junior doctor doesn't see another doctor's financials, and a visiting consultant shouldn't be able to delete patient records. Zonoir mirrors that reality in software. Every account is assigned exactly one role, and every database query is filtered against that role using · Row-Level Security (RLS) · at the backend — meaning permissions cannot be bypassed even from a custom browser or modified app. · The 5 roles in Zonoir · Roles are organised in a clear hierarchy. Each role inherits visibility only within its own scope — never across clinics. · Role · Who it's for · Scope · Admin · Zonoir platform team (us) · Entire platform · Clinic Owner · The person/business that signed up the clinic · All doctors, staff & records inside that clinic · Doctor · Practising physicians in the clinic · Their own patients, visits, prescriptions · Clinic Receptionist · Front-desk staff for the whole clinic · All doctors in the clinic (operational only) · Doctor Receptionist · A receptionist tied to one specific doctor · Only that doctor's patients & schedule · 1. Admin · The Admin role is reserved for the Zonoir platform team. Admins manage the public directory, approve new clinic and doctor signups, publish blog and SEO content, and handle billing escalations. · You will never need to create an Admin account · — this role is not available from inside your clinic dashboard, and Zonoir Admins never see patient medical data unless you explicitly grant access for support purposes. · 2. Clinic Owner · This is the most powerful role · inside your clinic · . The Clinic Owner is the account created at signup and is the legal Data Controller for every patient record stored under the clinic. · Clinic Owners can: · Add, edit, suspend, or delete · accounts. · Add, edit, or remove · Receptionist · View every patient record, visit, prescription, and invoice across all doctors in the clinic. · See the full · Finance dashboard · — revenue, expenses, net profit, doctor-wise breakdowns. · Manage the clinic's public profile, specialisations, schedules, and online booking settings. · Manage the subscription plan, billing, and trial status. · Export patient and financial data (CSV/PDF). · Clinic Owners cannot: · See data from · other · clinics on Zonoir — RLS blocks every cross-clinic query. · Sign prescriptions on a doctor's behalf (audit logs record the actual signer). · 3. Doctor · Doctors are the clinical heart of the system. Each Doctor account is attached to one clinic (or operates as a solo practitioner with their own clinic shell auto-created at signup). · Doctors can: · View and manage · their own · patient list, appointments, and visit history. · Write prescriptions, record vitals, attach lab reports, and use the AI Prescription Assistant. · Manage their own weekly schedule, breaks, and leave days. · Edit their public doctor profile (bio, photo, fees, specialisations). · Add medicines, allergies, diseases, ICD codes, and templates to the shared clinic library. · Conduct video consultations and review their personal performance analytics. · Doctors cannot: · See another doctor's patients, visits, or prescriptions — even within the same clinic. · Access the clinic-wide Finance dashboard (they only see their own earnings). · Create, modify, or delete other Doctor or Receptionist accounts. · Change the clinic's subscription or billing details. · 4. Clinic Receptionist · A Clinic Receptionist is front-desk staff who works for the · whole clinic · . They act as an operational deputy to the Clinic Owner for day-to-day patient handling — but with no financial or destructive powers. · Clinic Receptionists can: · Register new patients and update existing patient details. · Book, reschedule, or cancel appointments for any doctor in the clinic. · Mark walk-ins, check patients in, and collect consultation fees. · Generate invoices and print prescriptions / reports prepared by doctors. · View the clinic-wide appointment calendar. · Clinic Receptionists cannot: · Write or edit clinical notes, diagnoses, or prescriptions. · See the Finance dashboard, expenses, or net profit reports. · Create or remove staff accounts. · Delete patient records or visits. · 5. Doctor Receptionist · A Doctor Receptionist is tied to one specific doctor — common in setups where a senior consultant has their own dedicated assistant. Permissions are identical to a Clinic Receptionist, but · scoped only to that doctor's patients and schedule · . They will not see other doctors' calendars, patients, or appointments in the system at all. · This role is ideal for visiting consultants, partner doctors who share a clinic but operate independently, or hospitals where each specialist has a private secretary. · How permissions are enforced · Roles are not just UI hints — they are enforced at the database level. Every table in Zonoir has Row-Level Security (RLS) policies that check three things on every query: · Who are you? · (your authenticated user ID) · What role do you have? · (looked up from the secure · user_roles · table) · Which clinic/doctor do you belong to? · (your scope) · If any of those three checks fails, the database returns zero rows — even if someone tries to bypass the app and call the API directly. Their historical actions (prescriptions, invoices, audit log entries) are preserved for compliance, but they immediately lose all access to patient data. · Never share login credentials · — always create a dedicated account so audit logs remain meaningful. · Common scenarios · "I'm a solo doctor — do I need a clinic account?" · Yes, but it's invisible to you. text: Security & Compliance · Data Backups & Recovery · 8 min read · For Clinics & Doctors · Exactly how Zonoir backs up your clinic data, how long backups are kept, what you can recover yourself, and what to do the moment something goes wrong — from a single deleted patient to a full disaster scenario. · What you'll learn · Why backups matter for a clinic · In a healthcare setting, your records aren't just business data — they are a legal, clinical, and ethical responsibility. A lost prescription history can mean a missed allergy. A lost appointment book can mean a missed follow-up for a high-risk pregnancy. Zonoir treats backups as a first-class feature, not an afterthought: they run continuously in the background, are stored in encrypted form, and are tested for restorability on a regular schedule. · This guide walks you through every layer of that protection, what you can do yourself, and what to do if you ever need to recover lost data. · 1. Automatic daily backups · Every Zonoir clinic is protected by · automatic daily backups · of the entire production database. You don't need to schedule them, pay extra for them, or remember to "run a backup" before a big change — it happens silently in the background every day. · Frequency: · Full database snapshot once every 24 hours. · Encryption: · Each backup is encrypted with AES-256 before it is written to disk — the same standard used by banks. · Isolation: · Backups are stored in a separate, geographically replicated location from the live database. A failure of one does not affect the other. · Integrity checks: · Backups are verified after creation; a corrupted backup file would be detected and re-taken. · Plain English: · Every patient record, appointment, prescription, and invoice you saw at midnight is captured in a sealed, encrypted snapshot — ready to be restored if anything ever goes wrong. · 2. Point-in-time recovery (last 7 days) · Daily snapshots are useful, but they can only restore your data to "midnight yesterday". For finer-grained recovery, Zonoir keeps a continuous · transaction log · for the last 7 days. This unlocks · Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) · With PITR, we can rewind your clinic's database to any specific moment in the last week — for example, "3:42 PM on Tuesday, right before the bulk delete". This is the single most powerful safety net in the system. · What PITR can fix · A receptionist accidentally deleted 50 patient records this morning. · A bad CSV import overwrote correct phone numbers with junk. · A doctor account was deleted along with all linked appointments. · An incorrect bulk update changed every fee to Rs. 0. · What PITR cannot fix · Data lost more than 7 days ago (we fall back to daily snapshots for those). · Files that were never saved into Zonoir in the first place (e.g. lab reports kept only on a personal laptop). · Actions performed correctly but later regretted — restoring rolls back · every · change made by every user after that point. · 3. File & document backups · Lab reports, prescription PDFs, profile photos, and any patient document you upload to Zonoir are stored in · redundant object storage · — not on the same drive as the database. This gives them their own backup lifecycle: · Redundancy: · Every file is stored on multiple physical disks in different locations. A single disk failure cannot lose your scan. · Versioning: · When a file is overwritten or deleted, the previous version is retained for a recovery window, so accidental overwrites are reversible. · Signed URLs: · Download links expire automatically — but the underlying file in storage is preserved independently of those links. · 4. Retention & deletion timelines · Backups are not kept forever — that would be both expensive and a privacy risk. Zonoir follows a tiered retention schedule designed to balance recoverability with patient privacy rights. · Backup type · Frequency · Retention · Continuous transaction log (PITR) · Real-time · Last 7 days · Daily full snapshot · Every 24 hours · 30 days · Weekly archive · Every Sunday · 90 days · File storage versions · On every write · When you request account deletion, your live data is purged immediately and your backups roll off within the retention window above — after which your clinic's data is gone from every Zonoir system. · 5. What you can recover yourself — CSV & PDF exports · You don't need to wait for support for everyday backups. Zonoir gives every clinic and doctor self-service export tools so you can keep your own offline copies whenever you want. · Patient list · Go to · Patients → Export · to download your entire patient database as a CSV file (name, contact, CNIC, gender, DOB, medical summary). · Use this monthly as your own offline safety net. · See the · Importing & Exporting Patients (CSV) · guide for the exact column format. · Appointments & finance · Appointment Calendar → · filter by date range and export the table. · Reports → Financial Reports → · download monthly P&L, revenue, and expense reports as CSV or PDF. · Invoices → · each appointment invoice can be printed or saved as PDF for your own archive. · Prescriptions & visit notes · Every visit's prescription is printable and savable as PDF from the patient timeline. · For a full patient handover, open the patient profile and use · Print Full History · Recommended habit: · Export your patient CSV on the 1st of every month and store it in your own Google Drive or external drive. It takes 30 seconds and adds a second, independent layer of safety on top of our server-side backups. · 6. How to request a restore · Server-side restores (PITR or full snapshot) are not self-service — they have to be performed carefully by the Zonoir engineering team to avoid making things worse. Here's exactly how to request one and what to expect. · Step-by-step · Stop making changes · in the affected area immediately. This article is educational only and does not constitute legal advice — please consult a qualified healthcare attorney in your jurisdiction. · 1. What Are HIPAA and GDPR? · Both laws exist for the same reason: to protect sensitive information about real people. They apply differently based on · where your patients live · , not where your clinic is located. · HIPAA — Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act · Where it applies: · United States · What it protects: · Protected Health Information (PHI) — anything that identifies a patient combined with a health detail (name + diagnosis, phone + prescription, etc.) · Who it applies to: · "Covered Entities" (clinics, doctors, hospitals, insurers) and their "Business Associates" (software vendors, billing services) · Core rules: · Privacy Rule (who can see PHI), Security Rule (how PHI is protected technically), Breach Notification Rule (what to do if data leaks) · GDPR — General Data Protection Regulation · European Union, EEA, and UK (via UK GDPR) — regardless of where your clinic is located, if you treat EU residents, it applies to you · All personal data, with health data classified as a "special category" requiring extra protection · Core principles: · Lawful basis for processing, purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality, and accountability · Patient rights: · Access, rectification, erasure ("right to be forgotten"), portability, restriction, objection · 2. Do These Laws Apply to My Clinic? · Zonoir is primarily used by clinics in Pakistan and other non-US/non-EU regions. headings: How the Heatmap Is Laid Out
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · Peak Hours Heatmap Explained · 6 min read · The Peak Hours Heatmap turns your appointment history into a color-coded calendar grid so you can see — at a glance — which hours and days are busiest, when chairs sit empty, and where small schedule tweaks can unlock more revenue without adding doctors. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Scroll to the · Peak Hours Heatmap · card. Clinic owners see every doctor combined by default; doctors see only their own booked slots. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide heatmap but cannot filter down to individual doctors unless the clinic owner has enabled that permission in Settings → Roles. · How the Heatmap Is Laid Out · Rows · — Days of the week: Monday through Sunday. · Columns · — Hours of the day, typically 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM, in 15-minute or 1-hour blocks depending on your zoom setting. · Color intensity · — Darker or more saturated cells mean more appointments (or more revenue) booked in that slot. · Empty / pale cells · — Few or no bookings. These are your quiet windows. · Numbers inside cells · — Optional. Toggle them on to see exact appointment counts or estimated revenue for that hour. · What the Colors Mean · The heatmap uses a continuous color scale. Think of it like a weather map: cool colors are calm, warm colors are busy. · Color Band · Typical Meaning · What to Do · Pale / light blue · 0–1 appointment per slot · Consider trimming hours, running a promo, or using the slot for admin work · Yellow / amber · Moderate load, 2–4 appointments · Healthy baseline; monitor for growth · Orange · Busy, 5–7 appointments · Add buffer time, confirm pre-visit payments, avoid overbooking · Deep red / crimson · Very busy, 8+ appointments or at capacity · Open a parallel chair, extend the day, or add a doctor before patients wait too long · Color thresholds auto-adjust to your clinic's normal volume. A small one-doctor clinic will turn red at 4 appointments, while a multi-doctor hospital may not turn red until 15+. The scale is relative to your own data, not a generic benchmark. · What Data Feeds the Heatmap · Every confirmed, completed, or in-progress appointment contributes to the heatmap. Cancelled and no-show appointments are excluded by default so the map reflects real demand, not noise. · Data Point · How It Affects the Map · Appointment start time · Determines which hour / 15-min cell is colored · Doctor assignment · Filters the map when you select a specific doctor · Visit type · New, follow-up, procedure, or video — can be filtered separately · Status · Only Confirmed, Completed, and In-Progress count by default · Revenue mode · Toggle between appointment count and estimated revenue per cell · Reading Common Patterns · Once you know what to look for, the heatmap tells a story about patient behavior and clinic operations. Here are the most common patterns: · Pattern · What It Means · Suggested Action · Morning red, afternoon pale · Patients prefer early slots; afternoons are underused · Offer afternoon discounts or shift non-urgent follow-ups to afternoon · Monday and Saturday spikes · Weekend / start-of-week demand clustering · Add extra doctor hours on those days; lighten midweek · Same hour red every day · A popular doctor or a fixed popular time · Consider extending that doctor's shift or cloning their schedule · Random scattered hotspots · Demand is there but scheduling is inefficient · Tighten appointment rules, reduce walk-in chaos, use online booking · Whole day pale · Doctor is scheduled but not attracting patients · Review marketing, profile completeness, or consider closing that day · Red cells with long gaps beside them · Patients book around a specific event or doctor break · Move breaks to quieter slots; publish availability in larger blocks · Filtering and Zooming · Use the toolbar above the heatmap to drill into the exact view you need: · Date range · — last 30 days, last 90 days, last 12 months, or a custom range. · — isolate one doctor to see their personal peak and quiet hours. · Specialty · — compare demand across dermatology, gynaecology, dentistry, etc. · — new patients, follow-ups, procedures, or video consultations. · Revenue vs count · — count shows volume; revenue shows which slots are most valuable. · Time grain · — 15-minute, 30-minute, or 1-hour cells. Use 15-minute for fine-tuning; use 1-hour for strategic planning. · Using the Heatmap for Staffing · The heatmap is one of the fastest ways to decide whether you need more staff, fewer chairs, or simply a better schedule. Before hiring, ask: · Are the red cells caused by one doctor being overbooked, or by genuine market demand? · Are there pale cells immediately before or after the red ones where the same doctor could absorb demand? · Would adding 30 minutes at the start or end of the day clear the busiest block? · Which days have consistent low demand and could become half-days or admin days? · If red cells persist across multiple doctors and cannot be absorbed by shifting demand, that is a reliable signal that hiring or expanding hours will pay for itself. · Using the Heatmap for Marketing · Empty cells are not a failure — they are inventory. Run targeted campaigns to fill them: · Happy hours · — offer a small discount for bookings in consistently pale afternoon slots. · Same-day slots · — push notifications for open cells today or tomorrow. · Procedure days · — if Fridays are quiet but your equipment is expensive, promote Friday procedures. · New-patient windows · — reserve your red morning slots for follow-ups and use quieter slots for longer new-patient consultations. · Exporting and Sharing · Click · Export · to download the heatmap as a PNG image for team WhatsApp groups, or as a CSV grid (day × hour) for spreadsheet analysis. The PNG export is useful for morning huddles; the CSV export is useful when you want to model "what if" scenarios like adding a new doctor or changing slot duration. · Known Limitations · The heatmap uses historical bookings, not future bookings. It shows where demand has been, not what is scheduled next week. · Walk-ins are included only if they are logged in the appointment system as walk-in appointments. · Doctor leave and holidays appear as empty cells; do not mistake them for low demand unless the same pattern repeats outside holidays. · Color scales are clinic-relative, so comparing two clinics side by side requires reading the legend, not just the colors. · Related Reports · Appointment Status Breakdown · New vs Returning Patients Report · New vs Follow-up Appointments · Patient Drop-Off Reports · Doctor Performance Scorecard · Reading Your Analytics Dashboard · Pro tip: · Print the heatmap PNG and stick it in the reception area. Staff who answer phones and book appointments will naturally start steering flexible patients toward pale slots, balancing your day without any extra software training.

title: Patient Demographics — Gender, Age & City
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · Patient Demographics — Gender, Age & City · 6 min read · The Patient Demographics report breaks your patient base down by gender, age group, and city. It helps you understand who your clinic serves, where they come from, and how to tailor services, marketing, and staffing to match real demand. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Look for the · Patient Demographics · card. Clinic owners see data for the entire clinic by default; doctors see only patients they have personally consulted unless the clinic has enabled full-clinic visibility. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide summary but cannot export or filter by individual doctor unless that permission is enabled in Settings → Roles. · What the Report Shows · The report is split into three independent lenses. Each lens answers a different operational question and can be filtered by date range, doctor, specialty, and visit type. · Lens · What It Tells You · Typical Use · Gender · Male, female, and other / unspecified distribution · Plan gender-specific services, waiting-area layout, or marketing tone · Age · Patients grouped into pediatric, young adult, adult, middle-aged, and senior bands · Stock medicines, design preventive-care packages, set appointment durations · City · Which cities your patients are traveling from · Decide local SEO focus, outreach budget, or satellite clinic locations · Gender Breakdown · The gender chart shows the percentage and count of patients recorded as male, female, or other / unspecified. It is based on the gender field stored in each patient profile. · Count · — total unique patients with at least one visit in the selected period. · Percentage · — share of the total patient base for that filter set. · Unspecified · — patients whose gender was not captured during registration. A high share here usually means the front-desk form needs tightening. · Example: · A gynaecology clinic may see 95% female patients, while a general medicine practice in the same building might see a 55/45 split. Use the gender lens to set expectations for inventory like disposables, gowns, and sample medications. · Age Bands · Patients are automatically grouped into age brackets based on their date of birth. The default bands are: · Age Band · Range · Why It Matters · Pediatric · 0–12 years · Vaccines, growth monitoring, school-medicine demand · Young adult · 13–24 years · Lifestyle, acne, mental health, first-time consultations · Adult · 25–44 years · Chronic disease screening, family planning, career-related stress · Middle-aged · 45–64 years · Diabetes, hypertension, cardiac risk, preventive labs · Senior · 65+ years · Polypharmacy reviews, mobility support, longer appointment slots · Age is calculated at the time the report is generated, so the same patient may move from one band to another next year. Historical reports keep the band the patient belonged to during each visit if you filter by a past date range. · City Distribution · The city chart ranks patient home cities by count and percentage. It uses the city field from the patient profile, not the clinic's own address. · Top cities · — the five cities with the most patients are shown as a bar chart. · Other cities · — all remaining cities are grouped into an "Others" bucket. · Unknown · — patients with no city on file. A large unknown bucket means registration data quality needs attention. · Tip: · If a large share of patients is traveling from a neighboring city, consider adding that city to your public profile SEO keywords or running a targeted WhatsApp campaign there. · What Data Feeds the Report · Each lens is built from the patient profile and linked visit records. Only patients with at least one appointment or walk-in in the selected period are counted, so the report reflects your active patient base rather than every profile ever created. · Field · Used In · If Missing · Gender breakdown · Patient is counted in "Unspecified" · Date of birth · Age band calculation · Patient is excluded from age analysis · City distribution · Patient is counted in "Unknown" · Appointment / walk-in date · Determines whether the patient is included in the selected period · Patient is not counted at all · Filters and Date Ranges · Use the toolbar above the report to change the view without changing the underlying patient records: · Date range · — last 30 days, last 90 days, last 12 months, or a custom range. · — view patients seen by a specific doctor. · Specialty · — filter by the specialty under which the visit was booked. · Visit type · — new patients, follow-ups, procedures, or video consultations. · — focus the age and city charts on one gender. · Filters stack. If you select "Gynaecology," "Female," and "Last 90 days," every chart updates to show only female patients who had a gynaecology visit in the last 90 days. · Reading the Charts · Each lens uses a different visual so the insight is immediate: · Chart Type · How to Read It · Donut / pie chart · Slice size = share of active patients; hover for exact count · Vertical bar chart · Bar height = number of patients in each band; compare across bands · Horizontal bar chart · Longer bars = more patients from that city; "Others" groups smaller cities · Common Scenarios · Scenario · What to Check · Suggested Action · Pediatric share is rising · Age chart over last 6 months · Add pediatric supplies, child-friendly waiting area, and vaccination reminders · Most patients from one distant city · City chart · Run a weekend camp or partner with a lab collection center there · Unspecified gender is high · Gender chart · Make gender a required field in reception and online booking forms · Seniors dominate but slots are short · Age chart + appointment duration · Reserve longer slots for senior patients or add a dedicated geriatric hour · Female patients peak on certain days · Gender filter + peak hours heatmap · Align female-focused specialties with those days and promote them accordingly · Exporting and Sharing · Click · Export · above any chart to download a CSV or PDF. The CSV contains raw counts and percentages for each band, making it easy to build your own charts in Excel or Google Sheets. The PDF is formatted for printing and works well for clinic meetings, investor updates, or partnership proposals. · Known Limitations · The report counts unique patients, not visits. A patient who visits five times in the period is counted once. · Age bands are fixed. If you need custom bands, export the CSV and group the data yourself. · City values are taken exactly as entered during registration. Spelling variations like "Lahore" and "lahore" may appear as separate cities. Clean data in Patients → Profiles for the cleanest report. · Patients with no visits in the selected period are excluded even if their profile exists. · Related Reports · New vs Returning Patients Report · Top Cities & Patient Geography · Patient Drop-Off Reports · Peak Hours Heatmap Explained · Reading Your Analytics Dashboard · Pro tip: · Review the demographics report at the start of every quarter. A 15-minute review can reveal shifts in patient mix before they become staffing or inventory problems.

title: New vs Returning Patients Report
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · New vs Returning Patients Report · 6 min read · The New vs Returning Patients report shows how many of your appointments come from first-time patients and how many come from patients who have visited before. It is one of the fastest ways to measure patient acquisition, loyalty, and the overall health of your practice. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Look for the · New vs Returning Patients · card. Clinic owners see the full clinic view by default; doctors see only patients they have personally consulted unless the clinic has enabled full-clinic reporting. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide summary but cannot export or filter by individual doctor unless that permission is enabled in Settings → Roles. · How Patients Are Classified · A patient is counted as · new · for the selected period if they had their first ever appointment or walk-in with the clinic (or doctor) during that period. Every subsequent visit makes them a · returning · patient for that period. · Category · Definition · Counted As · New patient · First visit with the clinic/doctor in the selected period · One new patient, regardless of how many times they return later · Returning patient · Has at least one prior completed visit before the selected period · Every qualifying visit in the period adds to returning visit count · Walk-in · Unscheduled visit recorded through the walk-in flow · Treated the same as an appointment for new/returning classification · Important: · The report counts · patients · , not just appointments. A new patient who books three follow-ups in the same month is counted once as new and twice as returning within that month. · What the Report Shows · The report surfaces three core metrics that together describe patient flow and loyalty: · Metric · Meaning · Why It Matters · New patient count · Unique first-time patients in the period · Measures marketing reach and front-desk conversion · Returning patient count · Unique patients with at least one prior visit · Measures loyalty, continuity of care, and follow-up discipline · Return ratio · Returning patients total patients 100 · A healthy practice usually sees 40–70% returning patients · Reading the Charts · The report uses a combination of visuals so you can spot trends quickly: · Stacked bar chart · — shows new and returning counts side by side for each day, week, or month in the selected range. Useful for spotting seasonal swings. · Donut chart · — shows the overall share of new vs returning patients for the whole period. Hover over a slice to see exact counts and percentages. · Trend line · — plots the return ratio over time. A falling line means the clinic is acquiring new patients faster than it is retaining old ones. · Filters and Date Ranges · Use the toolbar above the report to narrow the view without changing any patient records: · Date range · — last 30 days, last 90 days, last 12 months, or a custom range. · — view new vs returning patients for a specific doctor. · Specialty · — filter by the specialty under which visits were booked. · Visit type · — in-person, video consultation, or walk-in. · Gender / age · — cross-filter with demographics for deeper insight. · Filters stack. Selecting "Last 90 days," "Dr. Ahmed," and "Video consultation" will show only new and returning video patients for Dr. Ahmed in that window. · Interpreting the Numbers · The right mix depends on your specialty, clinic age, and growth goals. Use these benchmarks as a starting point: · Return Ratio · What It Usually Means · Suggested Action · Below 30% · High acquisition but poor retention · Review follow-up reminders, discharge instructions, and patient experience · Healthy growth with room to improve loyalty · Introduce recall campaigns and membership plans · Strong loyalty and repeat care · Maintain service quality while testing new-patient marketing · Above 70% · Very loyal base, but acquisition may be too low · Invest in SEO, social proof, and referral programs to attract new patients · Common Scenarios · Scenario · What to Check · New patients spiked after a marketing campaign · Daily stacked bar chart during campaign dates · Track whether those new patients return within 60–90 days · Return ratio is dropping · Trend line over last 6 months · Audit wait times, billing disputes, and follow-up call completion · One doctor has far more returning patients · Filter by doctor and compare ratios · Study that doctor's communication style and share best practices · Video consultations have low retention · Filter by visit type = video · Add post-video care plans and scheduled follow-up links · New patient count is flat · Monthly new-patient trend · Refresh public profile, run a Google review campaign, or offer first-visit packages · Exporting and Sharing · Click · Export · above any chart to download a CSV or PDF. The CSV contains one row per patient with their classification, first-visit date, and total visits in the period. The PDF is formatted for printing and works well for clinic meetings, partnership reviews, or investor updates. · Data Sources and Accuracy · The report is built from completed appointments and walk-in records. A visit only counts when it has a status of · Completed · or · Checked Out · . Cancelled, no-show, and pending appointments are excluded. · Patients are matched by profile, not by name alone, so duplicate profiles can affect accuracy. · Merged patients keep their earliest visit date as the first-visit reference. · Walk-ins recorded without a patient profile are excluded until a profile is linked. · Related Reports · Patient Demographics — Gender, Age & City · Appointment Status Breakdown · New vs Follow-up Appointments · Patient Drop-Off Reports · Reading Your Analytics Dashboard · Pro tip: · Review this report every month alongside your marketing spend. If new-patient acquisition is rising but the return ratio is falling, you are filling a leaky bucket — fix retention before spending more on ads.

title: Appointment Status Breakdown
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · Appointment Status Breakdown · 6 min read · The Appointment Status Breakdown report shows how every appointment in your clinic ended up — scheduled, started, completed, cancelled, or no-show. It helps you spot scheduling leaks, measure front-desk efficiency, and understand patient flow at a glance. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Look for the · card. Clinic owners see the full clinic view; doctors see only appointments linked to their own profile unless the clinic has enabled full-clinic reporting. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide summary but cannot export or filter by individual doctor unless that permission is enabled in Settings → Roles. · Statuses Explained · Zonoir tracks four core appointment statuses. Each one tells you something different about what happened to the slot: · Status · Meaning · Counted In Report · Scheduled · Booked but not yet started · Yes — upcoming load and future capacity · Started / In Progress · Patient has checked in and consultation is active · Yes — current day activity · Completed · Visit finished and marked done · Yes — revenue and productivity base · Cancelled · Appointment cancelled before it happened · Yes — lost slot and possible rescheduling need · No-show · Patient did not arrive and status was marked no-show · Yes — when explicitly recorded as no-show · Note: · A single appointment can only have one final status. If a patient cancels and later rebooks, the original appointment stays cancelled and the new one starts fresh as scheduled. · What the Report Shows · The report surfaces the status distribution for the selected period and breaks it down so you can act quickly: · Metric · Why It Matters · Total appointments · All appointments created in the period · Baseline demand and scheduling volume · Completion rate · Completed total final-status appointments 100 · Core efficiency metric; most clinics aim for 80%+ · Cancellation rate · Cancelled total final-status appointments 100 · High rates may indicate overbooking or reminder issues · No-show rate · No-shows total final-status appointments 100 · Shows how many patients forgot or skipped visits · In-progress count · Appointments currently started · Live snapshot of today's clinic activity · Reading the Charts · The report combines several visuals so you can see both the big picture and the daily detail: · Donut / pie chart · — the overall share of each status for the selected period. Hover over a slice to see the exact count and percentage. · Stacked bar chart · — status counts grouped by day, week, or month. Useful for spotting whether cancellations spike on specific days. · Completion trend line · — plots the completion rate over time. A rising line means operations are improving; a falling line needs investigation. · Status table · — a sortable grid with counts, rates, and comparisons to the previous period. · Filters and Date Ranges · Use the toolbar above the report to drill into specific slices of your schedule: · Date range · — last 30 days, last 90 days, last 12 months, or a custom range. · — view status breakdown for a specific doctor. · Specialty · — filter by the specialty under which visits were booked. · Visit type · — in-person, video consultation, or walk-in. · — focus on one status, such as cancelled only, to investigate leaks. · Filters stack. Selecting "Last 30 days," "Dr. Khan," and "Video consultation" will show only the status breakdown for that doctor's video appointments in that window. · Interpreting the Numbers · Benchmarks vary by specialty and clinic type, but these ranges are a useful starting point: · Rate · What It Usually Means · Suggested Action · Completion rate above 85% · Strong scheduling and patient commitment · Maintain reminders and front-desk confirmation process · Completion rate 70–85% · Healthy but with room to improve · Review cancellation reasons and add pre-visit reminders · Cancellation rate above 15% · Patients are changing plans often · Send SMS reminders 24 hours ahead and confirm high-value slots · No-show rate above 10% · Patients forget appointments · Add WhatsApp reminders and consider a no-show policy · Started count stays high after hours · Appointments not being marked completed · Train staff to close visits before the end of the day · Common Scenarios · Scenario · What to Check · Cancellations spike on Mondays · Stacked bar chart grouped by day of week · Avoid overbooking Mondays; send weekend reminders · One doctor has low completion rate · Filter by doctor and compare status share · Check scheduling density, wait times, and patient feedback · Video consultations cancel more often · Filter by visit type = video · Send video-link reminders 1 hour before the call · No-shows rise after holidays · Trend line around public holidays · Run a reconfirmation campaign for post-holiday slots · Many appointments stuck on Started · In-progress count at end of day · Add end-of-day checklist to mark visits completed · Exporting and Sharing · Click · Export · above any chart to download a CSV or PDF. The CSV contains one row per appointment with its final status, date, doctor, patient, and visit type. The PDF is formatted for printing and works well for clinic meetings, partnership reviews, or operational audits. · Data Sources and Accuracy · The report is built from appointment records created in the system. Every status change is timestamped, so the report reflects the final status recorded at the end of the selected period. · Appointments must have a status other than draft to appear in the report. · Walk-ins are included if they were recorded through the walk-in flow and assigned a final status. · Deleted appointments are excluded entirely. · Status changes made after the report date range may shift historical numbers slightly. · Related Reports · New vs Returning Patients Report · New vs Follow-up Appointments · Patient Drop-Off Reports · Peak Hours Heatmap Explained · The 4 Appointment Statuses Explained · Pro tip: · Review the Appointment Status Breakdown every Monday morning. A quick glance at last week's completion, cancellation, and no-show rates tells you whether the coming week needs tighter reminders or schedule adjustments.

title: New vs Follow-up Appointments
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · New vs Follow-up Appointments · 6 min read · The New vs Follow-up Appointments report separates first-time visits from return visits for continuing care. It helps clinics understand how much of their schedule is consumed by initial consultations versus ongoing treatment, follow-up reviews, and chronic-care management. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Look for the · card. Clinic owners see the full clinic view by default; doctors see only appointments linked to their own profile unless the clinic has enabled full-clinic reporting. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide summary but cannot export or filter by individual doctor unless that permission is enabled in Settings → Roles. · How Appointments Are Classified · Unlike the · New vs Returning Patients · report, which looks at whether the patient has ever visited before, this report looks at the purpose of the appointment itself. Every booked or walk-in visit is tagged as either a · new appointment · or a · follow-up appointment · Category · Definition · Typical Examples · New appointment · First visit for a new complaint, condition, or referral · First consultation, annual check-up, new specialist referral, screening visit · Follow-up appointment · Return visit to review progress, results, or continuing treatment · Post-op review, chronic care monitoring, lab result review, medication adjustment · Unspecified / mixed · Visit type not recorded or visit spans both categories · Counted separately and excluded from the new/follow-up ratio · Important: · A patient can have a new appointment and a follow-up appointment in the same period. The report counts · visits · , not unique patients, so it reflects your actual clinical workload. · What the Report Shows · The report surfaces four core metrics that describe the shape of your clinical workload: · Metric · Meaning · Why It Matters · New appointment count · Visits flagged as first-time or new complaints · Shows demand for initial consultations and diagnostic work · Follow-up appointment count · Visits flagged as return or continuing care · Shows how much capacity is tied to ongoing treatment · Follow-up ratio · Follow-up appointments total classified appointments 100 · High ratios often indicate strong continuity of care · Unspecified count · Visits without a recorded new/follow-up tag · Flags data-quality gaps at the front desk or in booking forms · Reading the Charts · The report uses a combination of visuals so you can see both workload mix and trends over time: · Stacked bar chart · — shows new and follow-up counts side by side for each day, week, or month. Useful for spotting whether follow-ups cluster after specific procedures or campaigns. · Donut chart · — shows the overall share of new vs follow-up appointments for the whole period. Hover over a slice to see exact counts and percentages. · Trend line · — plots the follow-up ratio over time. A rising line means more of your schedule is being used for continuing care; a falling line means you are seeing more first-time visits. · Data-quality indicator · — shows the percentage of appointments that have a visit type recorded. Low coverage means the report is undercounting one or both categories. · Filters and Date Ranges · Use the toolbar above the report to drill into specific slices of your schedule: · Date range · — last 30 days, last 90 days, last 12 months, or a custom range. · — view the new vs follow-up mix for a specific doctor. · Specialty · — filter by the specialty under which visits were booked. · Visit type · — in-person, video consultation, or walk-in. · Condition tag · — filter by chronic condition, post-op, or other follow-up tags. · Filters stack. Selecting "Last 90 days," "Dr. Rizvi," and "Diabetes clinic" will show only the new vs follow-up mix for that doctor's diabetes appointments in that window. · Interpreting the Numbers · The ideal mix depends on your specialty, clinic model, and growth stage. Use these benchmarks as a starting point: · Follow-up Ratio · What It Usually Means · Suggested Action · Below 30% · Most visits are first-time; low continuity · Review discharge planning, follow-up reminders, and care-plan workflows · Healthy balance between acquisition and continuity · Maintain current follow-up protocols while monitoring data quality · Strong follow-up discipline; common in chronic-care specialties · Ensure capacity is not being squeezed by follow-ups; consider dedicated follow-up slots · Above 70% · Very high follow-up load; risk of long waits for new patients · Open more new-patient slots or add a junior doctor to handle routine follow-ups · Common Scenarios · Scenario · What to Check · Follow-ups spike after a surgical camp · Stacked bar chart around camp dates · Book post-op review slots in advance and send reminder messages · New appointments are rising but follow-ups are flat · Trend line and doctor-level filters · Audit whether follow-up recommendations are being recorded at checkout · One doctor has almost no follow-ups · Filter by doctor and compare visit-type capture rate · Train the doctor or receptionist to tag visits correctly during booking · Unspecified count is above 20% · Data-quality indicator and booking source · Make visit type a required field in online booking and walk-in forms · Video consultations have fewer follow-ups · Filter by visit type = video · Add video follow-up links and scheduled return appointments to care plans · Improving Data Accuracy · The report is only as useful as the visit-type data captured at booking. To keep the numbers reliable: · Train receptionists to ask "Is this a first visit or a follow-up?" for every booking. · Set the visit type default to unspecified so staff must actively choose new or follow-up. · Use appointment templates for common follow-up workflows so the tag is applied automatically. · Review the unspecified count weekly and correct miscoded appointments before month-end reporting. · Exporting and Sharing · Click · Export · above any chart to download a CSV or PDF. The CSV contains one row per appointment with its visit type, date, doctor, patient, and specialty. The PDF is formatted for printing and works well for clinic meetings, partnership reviews, or operational audits. · Data Sources and Accuracy · The report is built from appointment and walk-in records that have a recorded visit type. A visit only counts when it has a status of · Completed · or · Checked Out · . Cancelled, no-show, and pending appointments are excluded. · Walk-ins are included if they were recorded through the walk-in flow and tagged with a visit type. · Appointments without a visit type are counted as unspecified and excluded from the follow-up ratio. · Deleted appointments are excluded entirely. · Changes to the visit type after the appointment is completed may shift historical numbers slightly. · Related Reports · New vs Returning Patients Report · Appointment Status Breakdown · Patient Drop-Off Reports · Peak Hours Heatmap Explained · Reading Your Analytics Dashboard · Pro tip: · Review the New vs Follow-up Appointments report alongside your doctor schedules. If follow-ups are consuming prime morning slots, consider blocking late-afternoon or specific days for routine follow-ups so new patients can be seen sooner.

title: Patient Drop-Off Reports
text: Patient & Appointment Reports · Patient Drop-Off Reports · 6 min read · The Patient Drop-Off report shows where patients leave your care journey before reaching a completed visit. It helps clinics identify leakage points — from booked appointments that never happen to patients who visit once and do not return — so you can plug gaps and protect revenue. · Where to Find It · Sign in as a · Clinic Owner · Admin · , or · Doctor · and go to · Reports → Analytics Dashboard · . Look for the · Patient Drop-Off · card. Clinic owners see the full clinic funnel by default; doctors see only drop-offs linked to their own appointments unless the clinic has enabled full-clinic reporting. · Receptionists with reporting access can view the clinic-wide summary but cannot export or filter by individual doctor unless that permission is enabled in Settings → Roles. · What Counts as a Drop-Off? · A drop-off is any patient interaction that does not result in a completed, billable visit. The report groups drop-offs into four stages so you can see exactly where patients leave: · Stage · Definition · Typical Cause · Booked but not arrived · Appointment was scheduled but the patient did not show up · No-show, forgotten appointment, transport issues · Cancelled by patient · Patient cancelled before the appointment time · Recovered elsewhere, changed mind, scheduling conflict · Cancelled by clinic · Clinic cancelled due to doctor unavailability or emergency · Doctor leave, overbooking, clinic closure · One-time visit, no return · Patient completed one visit but never booked again · No follow-up plan, poor experience, moved away · Important: · The report lists up to the most recent 50 dropped patient records so the dashboard stays fast. For a complete historical list, use the CSV export or filter by a narrower date range. · What the Report Shows · The report surfaces five core metrics that describe the health of your patient funnel: · Metric · Meaning · Why It Matters · Total drop-offs · Count of patients who left the funnel in the selected period · Top-line indicator of how much potential care is being lost · Drop-off rate · Drop-offs total patient interactions 100 · Shows leakage as a percentage of opportunity · No-show rate · No-shows scheduled appointments 100 · Isolates the most common and most fixable drop-off stage · One-time patient rate · Patients with exactly one completed visit and no return new patients · Measures whether new patients are sticking around · Recovered patients · Patients who dropped off but later returned within the period · Shows the effectiveness of recall and follow-up campaigns · Reading the Charts · The report uses a combination of visuals so you can see both the funnel shape and trends over time: · Funnel chart · — shows how many patients move from booked appointments to completed visits. The widest section is booked appointments; the narrowest is completed visits. Gaps between sections represent drop-offs. · Stage breakdown bar · — splits drop-offs by stage: no-show, patient-cancelled, clinic-cancelled, and one-time-only.
